candidate.title: GMUCT 2.0
candidate.scope: The single GMUCT 2.0 schematic assigned to this card: poly(A) RNA selection, selective 5′ RNA adapter ligation, adapter-bearing random-hexamer reverse transcription and PCR indexing. The matching collection page captions this route GMUCT 2.0 and separately depicts GMUCT 1.0; that separate workflow, PARE, degradome sequencing and unshown adaptations are outside this extraction. The attached asset filename does not determine version scope. Reagent icons are components, and capped and uncapped RNA rows are molecular populations in one preparation, not alternative assays.

states.label: Degraded RNA population
features: The Degraded RNA panel shows an intact capped poly(A) RNA, a capped upstream fragment without a depicted poly(A) tail, and an uncapped downstream poly(A) fragment.
Purple lines denote RNA; AA(A)n denotes a poly(A) tail; 5′ GPPP marks the capped population. No experimental degradation operation is drawn.
The far-left Genome-wide mapping of uncapped transcripts (GMUCT) vignette repeats these populations and highlights the uncapped poly(A) fragment in yellow; it is an explanatory title icon.

states.label: Indexed cDNA library
features: The terminal label is Indexed cDNA; PCR provides sequencing indexes according to the caption and catalogue description.
DNA is the readout carrier for the selected uncapped/cleaved RNA ends; this is not a library of all polyadenylated RNA.
The captured population is constrained by poly(A) retention and a ligatable 5′ monophosphate; surviving these selections is not proof of a unique biological degradation pathway.

operations.description: Select polyadenylated RNA from the depicted degraded population. Both capped and uncapped poly(A) molecules survive; the non-polyadenylated upstream fragment is omitted from the retained material.
operations.mechanism: Selection by the poly(A) feature; no capture chemistry is specified in the drawing.
operations.information_effect: Restricts representation to retained polyadenylated molecules and fragments, rather than all RNA degradation products.

operations.label: Ligate 5′ RNA adapter
operations.description: Attach the green RNA adapter to the lower uncapped poly(A) molecule. The upper capped poly(A) molecule remains without this adapter.
operations.mechanism: The primary-paper abstract identifies T4 RNA ligase 1 and free RNA 5′ monophosphate as the substrate requirement; capped mRNA is not a substrate.
operations.information_effect: Physically marks eligible original RNA 5′ ends with an adapter junction. Decapped RNA and polyadenylated downstream cleavage fragments can be represented; this selection does not identify a unique decay or cleavage cause.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Use the Random hexamer fused to 3′ primer reagent to copy the selected RNA. The depicted productive output is adapter-flanked cDNA, with the opposite adapter supplied by the RT primer. Gray extensions are also drawn under capped RNA, but no capped-RNA product is routed to the final indexed library.
operations.mechanism: Random-hexamer priming introduces the primer’s 5′ adapter sequence during cDNA synthesis. The paired-strand icon is retained at schematic scope without inventing a separate second-strand reaction.
operations.information_effect: Transfers RNA sequence and its association with the ligated 5′-end junction into DNA. The primer supplies a library handle, rather than a second RNA-end ligation or full-length transcript guarantee. Random priming can also occur on capped RNA; the selective association is with the previously ligated 5′ adapter, not cap-specific reverse transcription.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and the collection’s GMUCT 2.0 caption identify the target. The adapter-bearing random-hexamer route distinguishes it from the separately described oligo(dT), fragmentation and subsequent adapter-ligation route of GMUCT 1.0. Applicability is resolved for this schematic, not every implementation. A second post-ligation poly(A) selection is described in catalogue text but not drawn, so it is not inserted as an operation.

checks.rationale: Independent image and source review supports the complete candidate at its declared schematic scope: seven material states, four local operations, ten material routes, the single GMUCT 2.0 target, and all three paper assessments. The candidate preserves schematic compression at cDNA formation and makes no full-text, historical-priority, interchangeable-method, or unshown adaptation claim. No consequential unsupported assertion or omission remains at this scope.
